text: Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin?
I'll search GEO for E. coli expression studies related to ciprofloxacin.

## Abstract

This report addresses whether the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) holds *Escherichia coli* transcriptional-profiling studies involving ciprofloxacin. A single query against GEO's Entrez `gds` index, restricted to *E. coli* as organism, ciprofloxacin as free text, and the GSE (Series) entry-type filter, returned 37 matching Series in total. The tool returned detailed records for the first 10 of these; the remaining 27 were not fetched. Among the 10 returned, several are directly concerned with ciprofloxacin as an experimental treatment rather than incidental mentions: GSE292923 profiles wild-type and ΔpurA *E. coli* before and after ciprofloxacin exposure (4 samples); GSE295494 captures time-resolved transcriptomes during early antibiotic exposure including ciprofloxacin arms (42 samples); and GSE275261 includes *E. coli* ciprofloxacin-treated samples alongside a GuaB inhibitor comparison (24 samples spanning two species). Others reference ciprofloxacin as a resistance endpoint (GSE309890) or as one of several perturbations (the GSE272158–GSE272161 nucleoid-organization Series). The result confirms that ciprofloxacin-focused *E. coli* expression data exist and are publicly retrievable. Because GEO's API returns metadata only, processed expression matrices reside solely in the FTP supplementary files listed per Series. The reported count reflects NCBI's MeSH-rewritten query, and the full enumeration of all 37 Series would require paging beyond this single call.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** *Escherichia coli* is a Gram-negative bacterium widely used as a model for antibiotic response. Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, triggering the SOS response and downstream transcriptional reprogramming. Transcriptomic studies of ciprofloxacin exposure inform understanding of tolerance, resistance emergence, and stress-response wiring. GEO is NCBI's primary repository for such expression data.

**Literature Review.** The GEO records retrieved carried linked PubMed identifiers, which I report as provenance rather than as papers I fetched in full text: GSE276254 (PMID 40879398), the nucleoid-organization SuperSeries and SubSeries GSE272158–GSE272161 and GSE283264 (PMID 40804527), GSE295494 (PMID 41805196), GSE292923 (PMID 42079445), and GSE275261 (PMID 39235234). GSE309890 had no PubMed link registered. I did not retrieve the abstracts or full text of these articles; only their GEO-linked identifiers.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before the query it was unknown whether GEO indexes *E. coli* ciprofloxacin expression studies, how many exist, and which treat ciprofloxacin as a direct experimental variable versus an incidental term.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: determine the presence and count of *E. coli* GSE Series matching ciprofloxacin in GEO, and identify which involve ciprofloxacin treatment directly. Expectation: at least several relevant Series exist.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO was selected because it is the repository holding processed bacterial expression data with organism and free-text filtering; no other resource on this question returns curated Series-level metadata.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO, reached through the `geo_search` tool against the Entrez `gds` database.

**Procedures.** One tool call:
- `geo_search` with `organism = "Escherichia coli"`, `term = "ciprofloxacin"`, `entry_type = "gse"`, `max_results = 20`.
- Executed Entrez term: `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND (ciprofloxacin) AND "gse"[Filter]`.
- NCBI query translation: `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND ("ciprofloxacin"[All Fields] OR "ciprofloxacin"[MeSH Terms] OR ciprofloxacin[All Fields]) AND "gse"[Filter]`.

**Statistical Analysis.** The total count (37) is the `total_count` field returned by Entrez esearch for the rewritten query. The response was size-capped by the server, so detailed records were returned for only 10 of the 37 Series; classification of "direct treatment" versus "incidental" below is based on reading the title, summary, and sample titles of those 10 returned records only. No deduplication or percentage was computed.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. *E. coli* ciprofloxacin GSE Series returned (10 of 37 total).**

| Accession | Title (abbreviated) | Taxon | Samples | Ciprofloxacin role | PubMed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE292923 | Effect of purA on transcriptome during ciprofloxacin treatment | E. coli | 4 | Direct treatment | 42079445 |
| GSE295494 | Transcriptomic responses during early antibiotic exposure | E. coli K-12 MG1655 | 42 | Direct treatment (cipro arms) | 41805196 |
| GSE275261 | IMPDH/GuaB inhibition in A. baumannii and E. coli | A. baumannii; E. coli | 24 | Direct treatment (Cipro comparator) | 39235234 |
| GSE309890 | Sertraline biases resistance emergence | E. coli K-12 MG1655 | 6 | Resistance endpoint | none linked |
| GSE276254 | Dual-mechanism antimicrobial peptide BTP-001 | E. coli | 51 | Resistance endpoint | 40879398 |
| GSE272161 | Elementary 3D organization (SuperSeries) | E. coli | 64 | Perturbation (cipro samples) | 40804527 |
| GSE272159 | Elementary 3D organization (MicroC) | E. coli | 33 | Perturbation (cipro samples) | 40804527 |
| GSE283264 | Elementary 3D organization (RNA-Seq) | E. coli | 25 | Incidental | 40804527 |
| GSE272160 | Elementary 3D organization (RedC) | E. coli | 4 | Incidental | 40804527 |
| GSE272158 | Elementary 3D organization (HiC) | E. coli | 2 | Incidental | 40804527 |

**Findings.** The query matched 37 *E. coli* GSE Series for ciprofloxacin. Detailed metadata were returned for 10. Of these 10, three treat ciprofloxacin as a direct experimental treatment of *E. coli* (GSE292923, GSE295494, GSE275261), containing 4, 42, and 24 samples respectively. Two use ciprofloxacin as a resistance-development endpoint (GSE309890, GSE276254). Within the nucleoid-organization study, sample titles such as `WT_cipro0025_MicroC` and `WT_cipro025_MicroC` indicate ciprofloxacin-perturbed samples in GSE272161 and GSE272159. The remaining 27 Series were not returned in this call.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met: ciprofloxacin-focused *E. coli* expression studies exist in GEO. The most directly relevant to a transcriptional-response question is GSE292923 (purA-dependent ciprofloxacin response) and GSE295494 (time-resolved early ciprofloxacin exposure), both of which name ciprofloxacin arms explicitly in their sample titles.

**Context.** The three direct-treatment Series each carry a linked PubMed identifier, indicating published or indexed work. The nucleoid Series form one SuperSeries family (PMID 40804527) in which ciprofloxacin is one of several DNA-affecting agents applied.

**Limitations.** The tool reported that the response was truncated: 10 of 37 Series were returned, so this is not a complete enumeration. The count of 37 reflects NCBI's MeSH-rewritten query, which expands "ciprofloxacin" across All Fields and MeSH Terms and may include Series where the drug is mentioned only incidentally. GEO returns metadata only; processed expression values exist solely in the FTP supplementary files, not in these records. Sample-level ciprofloxacin involvement was inferred from sample titles, not from verified per-sample protocol fields.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** At least 37 candidate Series exist, with a confirmed subset directly treating *E. coli* with ciprofloxacin. The next query worth running is a narrower search (e.g., adding "RNA-seq" or "tolerance") to reduce incidental hits, or paging the remaining 27 Series; then `geo_series` on GSE292923 or GSE295494 to locate the processed expression matrices for reuse.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, `geo_search` esearch query. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[2] GEO Series GSE292923. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/
[3] GEO Series GSE295494. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/
[4] GEO Series GSE275261. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/
[5] GEO Series GSE309890. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[6] GEO Series GSE276254. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE276nnn/GSE276254/
[7] GEO Series GSE272161. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/
[8] GEO Series GSE272160. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/
[9] GEO Series GSE272159. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/
[10] GEO Series GSE272158. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/
[11] GEO Series GSE283264. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/

## Acknowledgments

Data were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the depositing laboratories, accessed via NCBI E-utilities. PubMed identifiers were provided as registered in the respective GEO records.
